headline: Exploited at the edge, exposed at the core
standfirst: The exploitation pipeline is running ahead of patching. CISA has confirmed in-the-wild use of a critical Sangoma Switchvox flaw, a Citrix NetScaler authentication bypass is already being attacked, Chrome is shipping an emergency fix for an exploited V8 bug, and hundreds of thousands of attempts are targeting two WordPress plugins. Behind those sit a root-level Nexus 9000 vulnerability, a long-dormant PostgreSQL privilege-escalation path, a public CrowdStrike Falcon exploit, and a court-records breach with unusually sensitive exposure.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

If you run Sangoma Switchvox, start here. CVE-2026-9586 is a critical, unauthenticated SQL injection in the `/pa` endpoint that can execute arbitrary SQL against the backend PostgreSQL database, including operations that lead to code execution [[s7]]. CISA has confirmed exploitation in the wild and added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The affected on-premises range begins at 8.2.2.1 and ends before 8.4.0.2, and the catalog entry puts federal agencies on a fast BOD 26-04 remediation clock. For everyone else, the KEV listing is a signal to treat exposed Switchvox systems as an emergency patch rather than routine maintenance.

Citrix NetScaler is not in the KEV catalog yet, but it is in the same urgency class. CVE-2026-19490 is a critical authentication bypass affecting NetScaler ADC and Gateway, and it is already being leveraged in attacks [[s1]]. Because these appliances sit at the network boundary, an authentication bypass is often a foothold for further compromise rather than an isolated device issue. If you have not updated the affected 14.1 or 13.1 lines, treat any internet-facing NetScaler as potentially exposed. The absence of a KEV entry should not be read as reassurance: observed attacks are still the more authoritative signal.

Browser teams should push out the Chrome update immediately. CVE-2026-85046 is a type confusion bug in the V8 JavaScript engine, and a crafted HTML page can execute code inside the sandbox on versions prior to 152.0.7977.82 [[s21]]. The fix is already in a stable release, but exploitation is active enough that waiting for users to restart their browsers is the wrong approach. Enterprise patch tools should treat this as a forced update, not an optional prompt.

WordPress operators face a volume problem rather than a subtle one. More than 440,000 exploit attempts have been observed against two plugin flaws: a critical arbitrary file upload in Super Forms and a companion RCE issue in Elementor Pro [[s19]]. For CVE-2026-14894, the route is especially cheap. Missing file type validation and absent capability checks on an AJAX handler let an unauthenticated attacker mint a valid nonce in one request and upload an executable file in a second. Every affected Super Forms version through 6.3.313 is exposed. With that many attempts in the wild, vulnerable sites are being found by scanners, not by luck.

## Vulnerabilities

Cisco’s Nexus 9000 advisory is notable because it combines no authentication, remote access, and root-level impact. CVE-2026-20212 affects ten Silicon One-based Nexus 9000 switches and exists because TCP ports 43210 and 43211 are reachable in the default Layer 3 VRF [[s32]]. An attacker who can connect to those ports can send crafted input that executes with root privileges, and the same input can crash the S1HAL process and reload the device. Cisco has issued patches for the affected platforms, along with an IOS XR hardening release bundling seven umbrella CVEs, two of them rated 9.8. The lack of a workaround for any IOS XR version makes change windows painful, but leaving an unauthenticated root-level exploit exposed on network infrastructure is a bigger risk than a brief maintenance outage.

PostgreSQL administrators should look at CVE-2026-6471 even though it has been sitting in the codebase for twelve years. Dubbed PostGREShell, the bug turns a non-superuser account that holds the REPLICATION privilege into code execution as the operating system account running the server [[s12]]. The issue is missing authorization during logical decoding: the attacker can choose a decoding plugin that causes PostgreSQL to load an arbitrary shared library. That leads to arbitrary code execution, and the researchers describe a path to permanent superuser privileges and a persistent backdoor. Replication privileges are often treated as low-risk because they are not superuser, but this vulnerability shows how much trust that role actually carries. The fix is to upgrade to a patched release in a supported PostgreSQL branch.

The wildcard in this section is CrowdStrike Falcon. A public exploit named FalconFlank claims to escalate to SYSTEM privileges on fully up-to-date Windows systems running Falcon [[s8]]. There is no CVE attached and no KEV entry, so traditional vulnerability management will not flag it. If the claims hold, the impact is significant: the exploit targets a security agent that defenders rely on to catch everything else. The immediate step is not to wait for a scanner signature, but to assess which endpoints run Falcon, review available mitigation guidance from the vendor, and understand whether any local users already have enough access to attempt the escalation.

## Breaches

The Thomson Reuters C-Track incident deserves attention because court data is not ordinary PII. An unauthorized party obtained files from the court case management platform, which is sold through West Publishing, affecting courts in eleven U.S. states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario [[s34]]. A subset of the records may contain names and Social Security numbers, and the exposure of sealed court documents would create harm beyond identity theft, including risks to litigants, witnesses, and ongoing legal proceedings. Organizations using C-Track should treat the disclosure as a trigger to review which records were involved, whether local notification obligations apply, and what access controls exist around the most sensitive case files. For everyone else, it is a reminder that the justice system increasingly runs on commercial software with the same vulnerabilities as any other enterprise stack.

selected.title: Sangoma Switchvox Vulnerabilities Exploited in the Wild
selected.excerpt: Tracked as CVE-2026-9586, the unauthenticated SQL injection flaw can be exploited remotely for arbitrary code execution. The post Sangoma Switchvox Vulnerabilities Exploited in the Wild appeared first on SecurityWeek.

kev.shortDescription: Sangoma Switchvox contains a SQL injection vulnerability which allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements against the backend PostgreSQL database using a single crafted request, including database operations and remote code execution.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description: An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability exists in Sangoma Switchvox SMB Edition 8.3 (104997). The /pa endpoint processes XML content beginning with <PolycomIPPhone> and directly concatenates the user-controlled PhoneIP value into PostgreSQL queries without sanitization or parameterization. An unauthenticated remote attacker can execute arbitrary SQL statements against the backend PostgreSQL database using a single crafted request, including database operations and remote code execution.

selected.angle: CISA KEV confirms in-the-wild exploitation of a critical Sangoma Switchvox SQLi; the Sept. 5 remediation deadline makes patching urgent.

selected.title: Over 440,000 Exploit Attempts Target Super Forms and Elementor Pro RCE Flaws
selected.excerpt: Threat actors are exploiting two critical security flaws in WordPress plugins Super Forms and Elementor Pro, according to findings from Wordfence. The vulnerabilities in question are - CVE-2026-14894 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A missing file type validation vulnerability in Super Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload files of any type, including

nvd.description: The Super Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 6.3.313 via the submit_form function. This is due to missing file type validation and the absence of any capability check on the submit_form nopriv AJAX handler, whose only barrier is a session nonce freely obtainable by unauthenticated visitors via a separate nopriv endpoint. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The nonce requirement is trivially bypassed because the super_create_nonce nopriv AJAX action allows any unauthenticated visitor to mint a valid sf_nonce and session cookie in a single prior request, reducing exploitation to two unauthenticated HTTP requests.

selected.angle: More than 440,000 exploit attempts show attackers are mass-scanning for WordPress plugin RCE flaws in Super Forms and Elementor Pro.

selected.excerpt: Cisco has released patches to address a critical security flaw affecting 10 Silicon One-based Nexus 9000 switches that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute code as root, alongside an IOS XR hardening release bundling 7 umbrella CVEs, 2 of which are rated 9.8, with no workaround for any IOS XR version. nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the Silicon One integration for Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute code with root privileges.

This vulnerability exists because TCP ports 43210 and 43211 are accessible in the default Layer 3 (L3) virtual routing and forwarding (VRF). A successful exploit could allow the attacker to connect to an affected device and send crafted input that could be executed as code with root privileges. The exploitation of this vulnerability could also cause the S1HAL process to crash, which could cause the device to reload.

selected.angle: Unauthenticated remote code execution as root on Nexus 9000 switches is critical; apply Cisco's patches for affected Silicon One platforms.

selected.title: 12-Year-Old PostgreSQL Vulnerability Enables Database, Server Takeover
selected.excerpt: Dubbed PostGREShell, CVE-2026-6471 turns low-level replication access into code execution, permanent superuser privileges and a persistent database backdoor. The post 12-Year-Old PostgreSQL Vulnerability Enables Database, Server Takeover appeared first on SecurityWeek.

nvd.description: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL logical decoding allows a non-superuser holding REPLICATION privilege to dlopen any file visible to the operating system account running the server, via the choice of logical decoding plugin.  This in turn runs arbitrary code as that account.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

selected.angle: A 12-year-old PostgreSQL flaw turns replication access into code execution and superuser takeover; upgrade to patched branches.

nvd.description:
The web management interface in 
Tycon Systems TPDIN-Monitor-WEB2

stores and displays system credentials in cleartext on a certain configuration page accessible to authenticated users. Any party with access to the administrative dashboard can immediately read these credentials, which may be used to compromise other systems on the local network.

The web management interface of Tycon Systems TPDIN-Monitor-WEB2

 does not perform server-side validation of credentials during the login process. By submitting empty values for both credential fields, an unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the authentication check and establish a valid administrative session. This grants full access to device controls including power relay management, device reboot, remote access service configuration, and network settings, which could allow an attacker to disrupt connected infrastructure or cause physical damage to equipment.
